title: Senior's toolkit: async, timeouts and the network
summary: Timeouts, cancellation, combining promises and watching real requests: what keeps async code from hanging or crashing.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: async, timeouts and the network
steps.body: Async code in production fails in three ways: it hangs (no timeout), it crashes (an unhandled rejection) or it is slow (requests in series). These are the built-ins and tools seniors use to prevent and diagnose all three.

toolkit.what: A signal that aborts itself after `ms`. Pass it to `fetch` so a slow server can never hang your code. It rejects with a `DOMException` named `TimeoutError`.
flags: abort when either signal aborts (user cancel or timeout)
tell a timeout from a user cancel (`"AbortError"`)
toolkit.example: const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });

toolkit.what: JavaScript's `CancellationTokenSource`. Hand its `signal` to `fetch`, `addEventListener` or your own functions, and call `abort()` when the work is no longer wanted.
flags: cancel; awaiting code rejects with an `AbortError`
check it between steps of long work
throw the abort reason if already cancelled
toolkit.example:
const c = new AbortController();
searchBox.oninput = () => { c.abort(); /* start a new request with a new controller */ };

toolkit.what: Run work in parallel and get every outcome, even when some fail. `Promise.all` instead rejects as soon as one fails.
flags: all or nothing; fastest failure wins
`{ status: "fulfilled", value }` or `{ status: "rejected", reason }` for each
the first success; `AggregateError` if all fail
the first to settle, success or failure
toolkit.example:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(urls.map(u => fetch(u)));
const failed = results.filter(r => r.status === "rejected");

toolkit.what: A promise-returning timer, for retries with backoff and for tests. No hand-written `new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))`.
flags: a wait that can be cancelled

toolkit.what: Since Node 15 an unhandled promise rejection crashes the process. These flags show where warnings and rejections come from.
flags: print a stack trace for every process warning
raise every unhandled rejection as an uncaught exception, even when an `unhandledRejection` listener exists
log it with context before the process exits

toolkit.what: In the browser, watch every request: status, timing, headers, body. Most "the page is broken" bugs are visible here first.
flags: see how your loading states behave on a bad connection
make sure you see what a first visit gets
replay the exact request in a terminal or a bug report
toolkit.example: F12 > Network > Fetch/XHR > click the red row > Response

steps.prompt: What does this print, line by line?
steps.explain: Synchronous code runs first (A, D). Then the microtask queue empties (the `.then` callback, C) before the next macrotask (the timer, B), even with a 0 ms delay.

steps.prompt: Support reports that when the pricing service is slow, the checkout page shows a spinner forever. The code is `const res = await fetch(PRICES_URL);`. What is the senior fix?
options: `fetch(PRICES_URL, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) })`, then catch the `TimeoutError` and show a retry message
Increase the browser's default fetch timeout in settings
steps.explain: `fetch` has no timeout of its own, so a server that never answers keeps the promise pending forever, and `try`/`catch` catches nothing. A timeout signal turns the hang into an error you can handle. Racing against an already-resolved promise just returns immediately.

steps.prompt: Match each combinator to what it gives back.
pairs: every value, or the first rejection
a status object for every promise
the first success, or an AggregateError
whatever settles first, success or failure

steps.prompt: Give up on the request after 3 seconds, and tell a timeout apart from other errors.
code: const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.__1__(3000) });
steps.explain: `AbortSignal.timeout` rejects with a `TimeoutError`. A user pressing Cancel (`controller.abort()`) gives an `AbortError`, which usually needs no message at all.

steps.prompt: Which tool answers the question first?
items: Is the API returning 500, or is our code failing?
How does the page look on a slow phone connection?
A request must not wait longer than 5 seconds
Typing a new search should cancel the previous request
Five independent requests run one after another and the page takes 5x too long
Show a report even if two of ten sources failed

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Every network call gets a timeout and every promise gets awaited or handled: those two rules prevent most async incidents. When something is slow or broken in a browser, open the Network tab before you read code; it tells you which side of the wire the problem is on.
